newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Tuntex in $3.2 bln LNG storage plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Tuntex in $3.2 bln LNG storage plan - paper.

text.p: Taiwan's Tuntex would invest $3.2 billion to build a liquefied natural gas storage facility in the northern part of the island, the Economic Daily News said on Thursday.
The Taipei newspaper said Tuntex would invest NT$90 billion (US$3.2 billion) to build an LNG storage station with capacity to import six million tonnes of LNG per year.
The LNG facility would be built in Taiwan's northern Taoyuan county, which is home to one of the island's main crude ports operated by state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp.
Tuntex officials were unavailable for immediate comment.
Tuntex is a diversified company with a focus on polyester fibre, construction and investment.
It has growing investments in overseas petrochemical projects and ambitions to enter Taiwan's long-closed market.
To date, Chinese Petroleum is the only company allowed to import petroleum, including LNG, but under a liberalisation approved in 1996, the energy market is opening to competition.
Giant Formosa Plastics group will begin importing crude to supply its new refinery and petrochemical complex once the first phase of the US$9 billion project opens in 1998 or even in late 1997.
The government has not made clear when or how LNG imports might be liberalised.
